title: What’s new on Prime Video in November 2026, including ‘The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ Season 3 and ‘Campus Drivers’
summary: From the first authorized Muhammad Ali series to ‘Blade Runner 2099,’ here is everything coming to Prime Video this month, including NFL, NBA, and NHL games.

---


## Key takeaways


- The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power


returns for Season 3 on November 11.


- The Greatest


, the first authorized scripted series about Muhammad Ali, premieres November 4, and


Blade Runner 2099


arrives November 25.


- Live sports include


Thursday Night Football


,


NBA on Prime


doubleheaders every Friday, and Seattle Kraken hockey.


---


November on Prime Video brings one of the most anticipated returns in streaming.


[The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/lord-of-the-rings-rings-of-power-season-3-prime-video) is back for Season 3, premiering November 11, with Middle-earth plunged into all-out war five years after the fall of Eregion.


The month also features a stacked lineup of Prime Originals, including


[The Greatest](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/the-greatest-muhammad-ali-prime-video) , the first authorized scripted series about the life of Muhammad Ali, and


[Blade Runner 2099](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/blade-runner-2099-prime-video) , a new chapter set 50 years after the events of


Blade Runner 2049


.


Sports fans can catch


[Thursday Night Football](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/everything-you-need-to-know-about-thursday-night-football-on-prime-video) ,


[NBA on Prime](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/stream-nba-prime-video) Friday doubleheaders, and


[Seattle Kraken](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/seattle-kraken-games-prime-video-watch-stream) hockey throughout the month.


Prime Video is included with an


[Amazon Prime membership](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-prime-membership-worth-it) , which costs $14.99 a month or $139 a year in the U.S. Discounted memberships are also available for


[young adults](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-prime-for-young-adults) and


[qualifying government assistance recipients](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-prime-access-discounted-membership) . Check your local Amazon website for information on Prime membership pricing in your region.


Not a member yet? Start a


[30-day free trial](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-prime-free-trial) today.


Here’s everything that’s coming to Prime Video in the United States in November.


## Spotlight: ‘The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’


November 11.


In Season 3, Middle-earth is at war. Five years have passed since the fall of Eregion, and Sauron's armies have conquered all in their path. Few stand between the Dark Lord and total victory—Khazad-dûm, where the Dwarves are sealed within their mountain halls, and the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell, protected by their Three Rings. But deep in Mordor, Sauron toils obsessively, attempting to forge One Ring to rule them all.


## More Prime Originals


### **‘The Greatest’**


November 4.


The Greatest


is an intimate exploration of the incomparable life of the boxing champion, humanitarian, and global icon. Executive produced by Lonnie Ali, the wife of the late luminary,


The Greatest


is the first authorized scripted series about the life of Muhammad Ali, offering unprecedented access and going beyond the amazing victories and defeats that made Ali a legend, both in and out of the ring.


### ‘Terrell & T.O.’


November 5.


Terrell Owens defied expectations to become one of the most accomplished and polarizing players in NFL history. His physical dominance and theatrical flair redefined the wide receiver position, but locker room conflicts, media feuds, and over-the-top celebrations made him one of football’s most divisive figures. This feature-length documentary traces his extraordinary rise, the controversy that followed him at every turn, and his ongoing personal evolution.


### ‘Campus Drivers’


November 6.


Lois has it all: acceptance to prestigious Belrose University and her lifelong love, Max. Lane lives by his own rules: creator of 'Campus Drivers', the hottest app on campus, he is as famous for his smile as his refusal to commit. When heartbroken Lois shows up at his door, an unexpected cohabitation ignites an attraction that awakens buried wounds and changes everything.


### ‘The Chosen’ Season 6


November 15.


Season 6 of


The Chosen


captures the historic events of Jesus’ final day and how Jesus’ final hours changed the world forever. Pharisees call it justice. Romans call it peace. Followers call it murder. But in the face of loneliness and death, Jesus stands resolute in his plan that has always led to one place: the cross.


### ‘Madden’


November 18.


Inspired by the life of a beloved American icon,


[Madden](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/madden-movie-nicolas-cage-prime-video)


chronicles John Madden’s journey from a Super Bowl-winning partnership with Al Davis and the Raiders, to becoming football’s most recognizable voice, to building the worldwide


Madden NFL


video game. A celebration of a brilliant mind whose spirit, partnership with wife Virginia, and infectious love of people and football transcended sports.


### ‘Perfect Liars’


November 20.


Based on Alex Mírez’s Wattpad sensation with more than 140 million reads,


[Perfect Liars](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/perfect-liars-prime-video) follows Jude Derry as she enrolls at the elite Tagus University on a secret mission. Her goal: to infiltrate the powerful Cash brothers' inner circle and uncover the truth behind her brother's death. What begins as revenge becomes a dangerous web of seduction, secrets, and betrayal.


### ‘Clashing Through the Snow’


November 23.


A holiday snowstorm strands rival publishing editors Ryan Mitchell and Hannah Hendricks at the airport, forcing them into a shared rental car for a cross-country race to New York. With budget cuts threatening one of their jobs, every mile becomes a high-stakes showdown—until roadside mishaps, unexpected detours, and small-town charm melt the fiercest rivalry into something unexpected.


### ‘Blade Runner 2099’


November 25.


Fifty years after the events of


Blade Runner 2049


, Los Angeles has been reborn—just not by humanity. Fugitive Cora (Hunter Schafer), in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Replicant who is days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse their fragile city.


### ‘The Boy Who Stole Billions?’


November 30.


At 30, Sam Bankman-Fried ran a $32 billion crypto empire until he was convicted of stealing $8 billion in customer funds, one of the biggest frauds in U.S. history. For the first time, he tells his story from prison in this riveting three-part docuseries. Was it fraud, or did his risky bets simply spiral out of control? With never-before-seen interviews from those who built FTX with him, the series probes SBF’s pressure-cooker world, inner circle, and complicated relationship with his CEO and former girlfriend, Caroline Ellison.
